Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.

1. Heard Sri Rajat Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar Verma,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.
However, no one has appeared on behalf of the opposite party No.2/ complainant despite the notice having been served upon him/ her.

2. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant (Maina Devi) is languishing in jail since 24.06.2024 in Case Crime No.198 of 2024, under Sections 376-DA, 323, 342 & 120-B I.P.C.
and Section 5-J (ii)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Police Station-Sursa,
District-Hardoi.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as she has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution story so narrated in the First Information Report (in short F.I.R.).
4.

Attention has been drawn towards the impugned F.I.R. wherein the date of incident has been indicated as 30.10.2023 whereas the impugned F.I.R. has been lodged on 06.06.2024 pursuant to the application being filed under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. on 01.06.2024. without explaining the delay.
The present applicant is a lady, therefore, she may not be held responsible for the offence of rape.
So far as the allegation relation to Section 120-B I.P.C. is concerned, the same may be tested and verified during the course of trial.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant is having no previous criminal history of any kind whatsoever.

The charge-sheet has been filed and she undertakes that she shall co-operate in the trial proceedings properly and shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted and shall abide by all terms and conditions of bail order.

Besides, being a lady she may be given the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C.
6.

Per contra, learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the aforesaid prayer for bail of the present applicant by submitting that since the role of the present applicant was found in the commission of crime, therefore, she is not entitled for grant of bail, but he could not dispute the aforesaid contention of learned counsel for the applicant.
Accordingly, the instant bail application is allowed.

9. Let the present applicant (Maina Devi) be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on her furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Maina Devi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.
The applicant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.

10. It is made clear that since the present applicant has been granted bail considering the fact that she is a lady and she being a lady is given the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C., therefore, the parity of this order may not be claimed by the other co-accused persons.
[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.]
